item.title: Arizona Cardinals news: How would you grade Mike LaFleur’s first 5 weeks as head coach?
item.description: How would you grade Mike LaFleur’s first 5 weeks as head coach?
item.content:encoded:
We are five weeks into the Mike LaFleur era of the Cardinals and the team is sitting with a 1-4 record. After an impressive win over the Chargers in Week One (well, maybe not so much anymore), the team has lost four consecutive games and quarterback Jacoby Brissett has been up-and-down this year with three games over 270 yards passing and two where he failed to reach 170, including a 95-yard outing against Seattle.

There’s a lot working against LaFleur with the team’s personnel and talent at certain positions. That’s also not including the loss of left tackle Paris Johnson Jr. for the season.

Taking in all possible context, how would you go about grading LaFleur’s first five weeks of the season? How has he been compared to your preseason expectations?

item.title: NFL Injury Report, Week 6: Latest news, updates, fantasy football analysis for Lamar Jackson, Caleb Williams, more players
item.description: We go over the latest injury news and updates heading into Week 6, providing a list of players fantasy football managers will need to track.
item.content:encoded:
Week 6 of the 2026 NFL season is on the horizon and we're heading into our first big bye week slate. Four teams — the Bengals, Lions, Vikings and Dolphins — won't be playing, which will leave some holes in your lineup, on top of an ever-growing injury report. Below we'll provide the latest news, updates and fantasy football analysis for the Week 6 NFL injury report.

Quarterback

  • Lamar Jackson, BAL (ankle)

  • Caleb Williams, CHI (hamstring)

  • Michael Penix Jr., ATL (ribs)

  • Baker Mayfield, TB (thumb)

Jackson: The Ravens held Jackson out for their Week 5 win on SNF against the Falcons. Baltimore is hopeful Jackson can return for Week 6 in a key spot against the rival Browns. Tyler Huntley was capable in the comeback victory over Atlanta, finishing with 201 yards and two touchdowns, plus 20 rushing yards and a score on the ground. If Jackson sits, Huntley is a decent streaming option in fantasy, particularly with Jared Goff and Joe Burrow on bye.

Williams: The Bears could have Williams back under center in Week 6, per NFL Network's Ian Rapoport. Williams has missed the past three games with a hamstring strain and Chicago has gone 2-1 with Case Keenum and Tyson Bagent splitting time. Things got a bit ugly in Week 5 in a 31-7 loss to Green Bay. Bagent threw two INTs and just 87 yards before being benched for Keenum, who also threw a pick. If Williams can get back into the lineup, he's good to fire up in fantasy, and should be a boost to all Bears receivers against the Falcons in Week 6.

Penix: The Falcons lost Penix late in their OT loss to Baltimore on SNF in Week 5. Tua Tagovailoa came in relief and, well, did Tua things, throwing a game-ending interception in OT. The Falcons don't believe the injury is serious, but wanted to be cautious at the end of the game. If Penix misses games again, it could sink Atlanta's passing game if Tagovailoa is forced to start. Bijan Robinson would mostly be fine for fantasy as a clear elite RB1 but his ceiling may come down. Drake London takes the biggest hit if Penix is out.

Running Back

  • Saquon Barkley, PHI (hamstring) — Hopeful for Week 6

  • Quinshon Judkins, CLE (foot)

  • Kyle Monangai, CHI (toe)

  • David Montgomery, HOU (groin) — Considered week-to-week

  • Breece Hall, NYJ (quad)

  • TreVeyon Henderson, NE (ankle) — Out multiple weeks

  • Rico Dowdle, PIT (toe)

  • Will Shipley, PHI (foot) — Out multiple weeks

Eagles RBs: Barkley missed Week 5's brutal loss in London to the Jaguars. Shipley was injured during the game, paving the way for Dameon Pierce to lead the backfield. He mustered only 14 yards on 11 carries. If the Eagles can get Barkley back for Week 6 against the Panthers, great. But there's an issue of depth and the offensive line just lost Lane Johnson to retirement. If Barkley returns, managers can play him but know that his upside is severely lacking. Pierce is worth a waiver wire claim in deeper formats with Shipley facing a potential multi-week absence, but would be a risky flex option if Barkley sits again. Also be on the lookout for Philly to add a back via trade or the free agent pool.

Montgomery: The Texans' lead back was injured in Week 5's win over Tennessee and did not return. Head coach DeMeco Ryans told reporters that Monty "may miss some time" due to the groin issue. If Montgomery is sidelined, Woody Marks would take over as the RB1 for Houston and see the bulk of the touches in Week 6 against the Jaguars in London. Dare Ogunbowale would see some snaps as the backup. Marks would be a good RB3/flex option with RB2 upside. Week 6 is a tough draw against Jacksonville, but the Giants and Chargers are solid gets for Marks if Montgomery's injury lingers.

Henderson: It's been a rough start to his second NFL season for Henderson, who left early with an ankle injury in Week 5's blowout win over Las Vegas. Reports are saying it’s a high-ankle sprain, which will cause Henderson to miss multiple weeks. Corey Kiner got some mop up duty with Henderson out but it was mostly Rhamondre Stevenson getting the work meaningful work again. That had been the case, Stevenson leading the way with Henderson as the change-of-pace back. With Henderson out, Stevenson is an even safer RB2 option, especially the way the Patriots have rebounded the past two weeks. New England's schedule sets up well moving forward, making Stevenson an appealing trade target.

item.title: Most common players on eliminated teams from Week 5 in Yahoo Fantasy Death leagues — plus FAB waiver wire advice
item.description: Death Leagues have claimed more star players. Fantasy football analyst Scott Pianowski advises you on how to approach the waiver wire in Week 6.
item.content:encoded:
Every week I'll examine the most common NFL players on the teams eliminated in Yahoo Death Leagues, trying to figure out where the puck is headed. I will also offer some FAB advice ($1,000 cap is the Yahoo default), but please remember this area is highly context-sensitive and manager-specific.

Waiver strategy in Death Leagues

If you're new to this format, it's critical to understand that waiver strategy is significantly different in the world of Death Leagues.

You can often win a traditional fantasy league with modest help from the waiver wire, maybe a timely pickup or two. Sure, it's great if you crush the market and land the right guys — the best managers will always aim to be smart on the wire — but if your drafted team stays healthy and runs pure, some years that might be enough.

Immediate needs vs. playing the long game

In Death Leagues, the eventual winning manager will have assembled a MONSTER team at the end of the year, a juggernaut, a Pro Bowl-type of roster. And the way you build that beast is usually by having resources all season — not by using the majority of your FAB on a tantalizing early star. It's pivotal that you understand that the waiver wire should get stronger and stronger every week in Death leagues, because the eliminated manager is coming from a smaller and smaller league size every week.

Unless you have a draft touched by the fantasy angels, you are unlikely to win a Death League without a successful and careful waiver-wire strategy.

My Death League strategy is centered on the concept that I like my squad early in the year and I am confident I can beat at least one team per week while the field of opponents is large. Therefore, while I will dip my toes into the FAB market in the first quarter of the season, my primary goal is to keep major reserves in play for later in the year, when bye weeks hit and injuries are more prevalent — and the pool of opponents is smaller (so advancing is harder, in theory). Again, I urge you to remember: the waiver wire in Death Leagues gets stronger as the year gets deeper, a key reason to be judicious with your resources.

Not everyone will share my strategy, of course. If you want to chase major improvements and use the bulk of your FAB to load up quickly, then shoot your shot. Play the strategy you're comfortable with. Just understand that my recommendations are predicated on being careful early, and if you prefer something more aggressive, you'll have to jump the numbers up. You know your room better than an outsider does.

Keep in mind the bye weeks are here — the Vikings, Lions, Dolphins and Bengals don’t play in Week 6. When in doubt, we will prefer players with later bye weeks — if you survive deep in this format, your roster will be loaded in the money weeks (making byes less painful). October absences can be more difficult to negotiate.

Understanding FAB recommendations

I will offer weekly FAB recommendations in three buckets:

Proactive: This means you highly covet this player, perhaps might even need this player. I realize these offers might not win if someone in your league is lighting money on fire, but as described above, that's often a short-sighted mistake in this format.

Reactive: This means you desire the player but the offer has to make sense for your short- or long-term strategy.

Keep Them Honest: This is an offer that is not designed to win, but might surprisingly land a player if your opponents are distracted by other talent available or unexpectedly passive that week. I often compare notes with other experienced Death League players and we're surprised at how often the Keep Them Honest offers actually win (this is also a portable strategy for regular season-long leagues; you never know when strange market behavior will come about).

One last note: understand that the FAB recommendations are with the assumption that you won't be making offers for every available player.

1. WR CeeDee Lamb, Cowboys

Receivers are the boom-or-bust position in fantasy, exemplified by Lamb going off in Week 4 (17-189-1) and falling off in Week 5 (2-9-0). Lamb is also dealing with a quad injury, though it’s not thought to be serious. The Cowboys have a favorable Week 14 bye, so Lamb is worth an aggressive bid.

FAB Recommendation:

  • $250 proactive

  • $150 reactive

  • $75 them honest

2. RB Kenneth Walker III, Chiefs

Walker has been one of the home runs of the year, but a Week 5 bye caught some managers off-guard. He would be an easy first-round pick if we redrafted today, so pay up.

FAB Recommendation:

  • $270 proactive

  • $160 reactive

  • $85 keep them honest

3. RB Omarion Hampton, Chargers

I wrote a lot of pro-Chargers stuff in the summer, and I’d like to burn all of it. Cluster injuries on the offensive line haven’t helped, but Hampton did little with his 14 carries (33 yards) against Denver. The LAC backfield is now a three-headed monster, so good luck finding value here. The Bolts also have a Week 7 bye.

FAB Recommendation:

  • $70 proactive

  • $30 reactive

  • $5 keep them honest

4. TE Harold Fannin Jr., Browns

The New York defense and the New Jersey rain held Fannin back in Week 5, though Deshaun Watson and the Cleveland coaching staff did him no favors. Baltimore is probably a better matchup in Week 6. Fannin probably isn't a Tier 1 tight end this year, but he’s good enough to start in most formats.

FAB Recommendation:

  • $80 proactive

  • $35 reactive

  • $8 keep them honest

5. RB TreVeyon Henderson, Patriots

A first-half injury knocked Henderson out in Week 5, and we now know it’s a high-ankle sprain. He’ll miss multiple weeks, and that’s especially penal in this format, where we need to “Play for Today” at all times.

FAB Recommendation:

  • $30 proactive

  • $10 reactive

  • $1 keep them honest

6. WR Tetairoa McMillan, Panthers

He was unstoppable in Week 4 against Detroit (14-192-2) and at least his bye week is out of the way now. With Bryce Young improving, McMillan has a strong chance to beat — and maybe smash — his reasonable summer ADP.

FAB Recommendation:

  • $200 proactive

  • $95 reactive

  • $40 keep them honest

7. WR Tee Higgins, Bengals

He played in 69% of the snaps despite his groin injury, only a marginal drop from a regular week. His quiet game at Miami was mostly a story of variance. Given that Higgins isn’t completely healthy at the moment, the Week 6 bye isn’t unwelcome.

FAB Recommendation:

  • $110 proactive

  • $55 reactive

  • $10 keep them honest

8. RB Chase Brown, Bengals

He lost a fumble in the win at Miami and also lost more touches to Samaje Perine than anyone expected. Brown is still the lead back here, but perhaps not the bell cow we expected all summer. Brown takes his bye in Week 6.

FAB Recommendation:

  • $140 proactive

  • $65 reactive

  • $15 keep them honest

9. QB Tyler Shough, Saints

He bottomed out in Week 5, largely because of the Minnesota defense. But it’s possible an injury to Shough’s non-throwing hand is also bothering him. We should get a better read on things when Shough takes on the Giants this week, but he’s not an automatic starter in any format that requires just one QB.

FAB Recommendation:

  • $40 proactive

  • $15 reactive

  • $1 keep them honest

10. WR Romeo Doubs, Patriots

He had a splashy game at Buffalo in Week 4 (6-58-2), but there was a Romeo void in the win over the Raiders (1-16-0, just three targets). The current shape of the New England passing game doesn’t force the ball to any singular receiver, so Doubs is a depth-only piece right now.

FAB Recommendation:

  • $20 proactive

  • $5 reactive

  • $1 keep them honest

item.title: Getting Defensive: Week 6 fantasy plays led by Steelers, Jaguars; top streaming defenses
item.description: Gary Davenport breaks down the fantasy football defense landscape headed into Week 6 of the 2026 NFL season.
item.content:encoded:
Back in the 1960s and 1970s, NFL offenses were terrorized by “The Purple People Eaters,” a defensive front in Minnesota littered with Pro Bowlers and anchored by a pair of Hall of Famers in Alan Page and Carl Eller. That defense helped propel the Vikings to a quartet of Super Bowls.

Now, no one is comparing the 2026 iteration of the Vikings defense to those all-time squads. But five weeks into the season, Minnesota is one of three undefeated teams remaining—and that defense is the reason why.

After holding the Saints to just 142 total yards and 13 points last week in New Orleans, the Vikings are currently third in total defense, third against the pass, fifth against the run and lead the league in scoring defense at just 12.8 points per game.

As good as those numbers are, it’s Brian Flores’ aggressiveness as defensive coordinator that is giving fantasy managers the vapors. In an NFL where no other team is blitzing at a 48 percent clip, Flores is sending an extra pass-rusher over 72 percent of the time. I know I’ve mentioned this before, but that is a staggering number—and it’s working.

Five games in, the Vikings are tied for the third-most sacks in the league with 17. They are one of three NFL teams with double-digit takeaways. And the Vikings are leading all defenses in fantasy points.

They may not be The Purple People Eaters. But they have become an every-week must-start in fantasy leagues. Just not in Week 6—they’re on bye.

Fantasy Football Waiver Wire Week 6: Woody Marks and Germie Bernard step up
Germie Bernard and Woody Marks were thrust into larger roles than expected in Week 5. Both players will be asked to step up in Week 6, making them two of the best waiver wire adds this week.
  • Kyle Dvorchak,

THE NO-DOUBTERS

Pittsburgh Steelers (at Tampa Bay Buccaneers)

In news that should surprise very few people, the Steelers are once again a top-five fantasy defense in 2026. But last week’s effort against the Indianapolis Colts was the team’s worst of the season—a single Cameron Heyward sack and no takeaways. T.J. Watt and the Steelers will get back on track this week in Tampa—last week’s win in Dallas aside, the last time rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels faced an actual NFL defense he struggled mightily, and no team has given up more fantasy points per game to defenses this year than the Buccaneers.

Jacksonville Jaguars (vs. Houston Texans—London)

No, the Jaguars aren’t moving across The Pond—at least not yet. But for the second week in a row, the AFC’s highest scoring fantasy defense will “host” a team in London, this time their AFC South rivals. This isn’t about the matchup—the Texans actually rank in the bottom-10 in fantasy points per game allowed to defenses. This about an excellent Jaguars defense that won’t have its routine disrupted this week. Jacksonville may be the AFC’s best team—and their balance is a big reason why.

San Francisco 49ers (vs. Washington Commanders)

If you know how the San Francisco 49ers are still undefeated despite a never-ending onslaught of injuries, explain it to me like I’m five. Despite being down their best edge-rusher in Seattle, the Niners sacked Sam Darnold five times, turned the Seahawks over four times and scored a defensive touchdown. At home? In primetime? Against the floundering Commanders. Top-five numbers. Book it. Wait, being that confident makes me nervous. You know what? Never mind. Double-book it.

Kansas City Chiefs (vs. Los Angeles Chargers)

From all indications, the Chiefs are back, and they come out of their bye week with a healthy Patrick Mahomes and a defense that ranks seventh in the league in points allowed. Across the AFC West in Los Angeles, the Chargers have completely imploded—the winless Bolts have no offensive identity, a rattled and beaten quarterback and an offense that is 25th in yards per game, 30th in points per game and second in fantasy points per game surrendered to opposing defenses. Heads roll in L.A. after the Chiefs roll at Arrowhead.

Seattle Seahawks (at Denver Broncos)

The bad news is that the Seahawks have to travel on a short week after a devastating loss to the 49ers at home to face a dangerous Denver Broncos team. But Seattle’s “Dark Side” defense has been consistently productive outside whatever the heck happened in Washington, including three sacks and three takeaways last week against San Francisco. The Broncos are having all kinds of trouble running the ball, and if they are forced to be one-dimensional Bo Nix had best wear comfortable shoes.

Fantasy Football Kicker Streamers: The 3 best pickups for Week 6
Cairo Santos is among the waiver wire options in a good spot headed into Week 6.
  • Denny Carter,

STREAMERS OF THE WORLD, UNITE!

Baltimore Ravens (at Cleveland Browns)

The Ravens may be 4-1, but the revamped defense bears just enough similarities to last year’s squad to make Baltimore fans uneasy. Still, that defense was OK in Atlanta last week with three sacks and a pick, and it should be far easier sledding in Week 6. Cleveland’s run game is among the NFL’s worst when Quinshon Judkins is healthy, and Cleveland quarterback Deshaun Watson was dropped eight times a week ago by the dominant pass rush (snicker) of the New York Jets.

Los Angeles Rams (vs. Arizona Cardinals)

Whatever tiny flecks of shine were left on one of the summer’s highest-drafted defenses were surgically removed by Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills on Monday night—you’d think we’d learn about “Dream Team” situations, and yet we do not even a little because people. But at 2-3 after a truly brutal schedule to start the season, the Rams finally get a break against a Cardinals team that just got smoked at home by the Lions. The Rams need this win—badly. And the Cardinals will pay the price.

New England Patriots (vs. New York Jets)

In the words of Samuel Clemens, it appears that reports of the demise of the New England Patriots have been exaggerated. The Patriots are quietly fifth in the league in yards allowed and fourth in the league in points allowed. Outside a huge outing at home against the Steelers that hasn’t really equated to fantasy points though, which has knocked them into streamer territory—a good place to be ahead of a Week 6 home date with a Jets team that has struggled mightily with offensive consistency this season.

New York Giants (vs. New Orleans Saints)

The Giants are quietly eighth in fantasy points among defenses after five weeks, despite being average in most statistical categories. There hasn’t been one massive week, one OK one and three duds, either—the Giants somehow find a way to at least get fantasy managers something, including five sacks in another bizarre game in D.C. (What is up in that stadium? Inter-dimensional vortex?). Add in a top-10 fantasy matchup for the position with the reeling Saints, and you have the definition of a matchup start.

Indianapolis Colts (vs. Tennessee Titans)

This is one of those “my defense is on bye and every other team in my league has two” type of plays—the Colts just got cooked on the road by the offensive juggernaut that is the Pittsburgh Steelers and have recorded negative fantasy points in two of five games this year in some scoring systems. But the Colts are at home facing a Tennessee Titans offense that is truly offensive—the Titans are the only team in the NFL averaging less than 250 yards of offense and 12 points per game.

item.title: Vic Fangio confirms Eagles will rotate Jeremiah Trotter Jr. and Jihaad Campbell moving forward
item.description: The Eagles’ 2025 first-round pick will be losing snaps to his backup.
item.content:encoded:
The Philadelphia Eagles entered Week 5 planning to make a change at off-ball linebacker.

That plan went out of the window after Jeremiah Trotter Jr. was questionably ejected for an on-field fracas that took place during the game’s opening kickoff.

As revealed by Zack Baun (via the Inquirer), the plan was to have Jihaad Campbell and Jeremiah Trotter Jr. rotate at the linebacker spot next to the Eagles’ All-Pro starter.

There was also a curious mention on the game’s broadcast about Trot Jr. potentially starting the game. Speaking during his Tuesday morning press conference, Eagles defensive coordinator denied that was the case:

“That is an out-and-out lie. Never said that.”

Fangio did, however, confirm the Eagles’ plan to get Trotter more involved:

“Yeah, we were going to play Trotter some.”

There have been calls (including here at Bleeding Green Nation) for Trot Jr. to see more snaps with Campbell struggling this season as he also plays through a knee injury.

Asked for his evaluation of Campbell’s most recent performance, Fangio replied:

“Played OK. Played OK.”

Fangio was asked about the impetus for the change. His answer:

“Well, Trot played good in the start that he had when Zack [Baun] was out. It was a close. I just think he deserves playing time.”

Fangio said the rotation will go “by series” as opposed to specific game situations.

Fangio is typically not shy to put what he feels are his best players on the field, regardless of their status. He clearly didn’t want to play Bryce Huff, the Eagles’ first and most expensive offseason signing in 2024, despite the front office’s investment in him.

Now Fangio is putting the Eagles’ first-round pick from the 2025 NFL Draft in a situation where he’s going to lose playing time to his backup. One can only wonder if it’s a matter of time before Trot Jr. fully takes over. Or perhaps it’ll truly be a time-share the rest of the way.

We’ll see.

I don’t disagree that Trot Jr. deserves more playing time; he’s good and he often knows where to be. But he does have some athletic limitations that have prevented him from earning a start job sooner. He also notably missed a key tackle on Kyren Williams that allowed the Los Angeles Rams to score the game-winning touchdown in Week 4. He’s not perfect. But there is intrigue to be had with his upside.

And now we’ll be able to see how he fares with more playing time.

item.title: Kyle Shanahan praises Raheem Morris for providing critical confidence boost
item.description: The 49ers head coach identified the area where the defensive coordinator has had the most significant influence.
item.content:encoded:
With the 49ers coming off their best defensive performance of the season in their biggest game of the year so far, it’s no surprise there is a lot of praise coming the way of coordinator Raheem Morris.

The 49ers’ outstanding defensive showing in the thrilling win over the Seattle Seahawks — which saw San Francisco force four turnovers, sack Sam Darnold five times and restrict Seattle to a 30 percent success rate — was one in which every area of the defense excelled.

San Francisco’s front consistently won when defending both the run and the pass, the linebacker play was typically excellent, and the secondary’s ascension continued as the defensive backs thrived in coverage, albeit against a Seahawks receiving group light on difference-makers outside of the not fully healthy Jaxon Smith-Njigba.

Through five games, the 49er defense has taken huge strides after what could at best be described as a below-par year with Robert Saleh as coordinator in 2025, though Saleh was hamstrung by a huge amount of injury adversity.

Following the display in Seattle, that improvement is reflected by the numbers, with the San Francisco defense third in the NFL by Expected Points Added per play and eighth in the NFL by success rate.

Morris’ fingerprints are all over the progress made by the 49er defense, but, speaking in his Monday conference call, head coach Kyle Shanahan identified where the former Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Atlanta Falcons head coach has arguably made the biggest difference.

Shanahan said:

“It doesn’t surprise me with Raheem. I’ve just been around him for too long. He’s one of the best people and best coaches I’ve ever been around. I tried to bring him here originally when I left Atlanta. They wouldn’t let him out. So, it’s been a long time coming to get him here. He’s done an unbelievable job this year, especially with the injuries, but just overall everything he’s mixed up schematically. I love the confidence he’s given our DBs and the way they’ve been playing since training camp. He’s had a real huge effect on this team and we’re very lucky to have him.”

With an extensive background of coaching defensive backs in his career, the 49ers will have entered the year hoping Morris could have a transformative influence on their secondary.

To this point, those hopes have been realized and then some.

Renardo Green is enjoying a breakout year at cornerback. His three interceptions in five games mark a career-high following his pair in Seattle and his passer rating when targeted of 45.0 is seventh among all corners.

Deommodore Lenoir’s numbers aren’t as impressive, but his lockdown performance against Courtland Sutton was key to the 49ers’ Week 4 win over the Denver Broncos. In addition, the play at safety through five weeks has served to allay concerns about San Francisco’s options at that spot, with Marques Sigle, Ji’Ayir Brown and Malik Mustapha all producing impressive play in varying amounts of time on the field.

The challenge for the secondary and the defense overall will be to maintain this tremendous start. Given the difficulty of playing cornerback and secondary, there will clearly be ups and downs. However, if the defensive backfield can maintain a relative level of consistency, Morris’ unit should be in good shape to stay in the upper echelons of the league.

For this young defense to regularly play at the level they produced in Week 5 will be a big ask, but in Morris, they look to have exactly the right mentor.

item.title: Mike Pettine could have a bigger influence on defense than advertised
item.description: What type of role do you think Mike Pettine is going to play?
item.content:encoded:
Before Dallas Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer left the podium Thursday night after the embarrassing loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, he said the team is being evaluated at all levels for potential change. After the mini-bye week, Dallas made a big change, or more specifically addition.

The team is hiring long-time NFL coach Mike Pettine as a senior defensive assistant. Pettine was one of Christian Parker’s mentors during his time with the Green Bay Packers, so the two know each other. When Parker was hired in Dallas, Todd Archer spoke with Pettine about what he learned about Parker, who was 28 at the time, while they worked together.

“From the jump, when you spend time around him, you realize he’s much more mature than what his age is, especially from a football standpoint,” Pettine said. “He had a lot of good input but didn’t force it on the room. He and I spent a lot of time together because he would do the game-plan drawings. If we had an issue with a formation or a defense we put together, he had input and he’s not just doing the drawing. You’re recognizing pretty quickly there’s an ‘it,’ factor with him.”

“There were certain things I wanted from him that would be hard to see from the sideline, and he was always good with those things,” Pettine said. “He was good at ‘What can we do?’ and ‘What can’t we do?’ Again, he was a QC with us, but he definitely had my ear.”

With the Cowboys’ defense sitting last in many categories over a month into the season, they looked outside the building for a former mentor to bring a new voice to the room. Parker wanted to bring Pettine on as a consultant after he was hired, but the former defensive coordinator wanted to stay retired. There was an open invitation to jump on board.

Now that the invitation has been checked “yes,” the Cowboys have someone to help guide Parker through the rest of the season and help the young coordinator regain his footing that made him a qualified candidate in the first place. Ed Werder adds context, suggesting Pettine could end up with a bigger voice in the room than the team is presenting.

In the days since Thursday night’s loss, Jerry Jones and Schottenheimer have reaffirmed their belief in Parker as the guy to lead their defense. Outside of letting go of Parker, this was the right move for the Cowboys. It comes at a good time because, with the Green Bay Packers coming up this weekend, Pettine’s last two years in the NFL were spent with Matt LaFleur and the Packers.

The NFC East is up for the taking. The Philadelphia Eagles are on a three-game losing streak, the New York Giants might not sustain the Jameis Winston magic for long, and the Washington Commanders look on the verge of breaking.

If Pettine gets more of a voice in defensive meetings and takes some responsibility off Parker’s shoulders, applaud the Cowboys for making a move to improve their team and address a desperate need. Parker’s specialty is with the secondary, so maybe with Pettine in the building, Parker can spend more time with DaRon Bland and others to help improve the league’s worst defense in EPA per play.

item.title: How the Denver Broncos can beat the Seattle Seahawks
item.description: The Denver Broncos host the Seattle Seahawks in Week 6 on Thursday Night Football. Here are three things the Broncos must accomplish to defeat the defending Super Bowl champions.
item.content:encoded:
The Denver Broncos host the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks on Thursday Night Football. The Broncos are coming off a close victory over the Los Angeles Chargers. Meanwhile, the Seahawks are looking to rebound after losing a nailbiter to the San Francisco 49ers. In order to topple the Seahawks in primetime, here are three things the Broncos have to accomplish.

No more excuses: It’s time for Bo Nix to rip it and deliver through the air

There is no doubt the offense has drastically taken a step back five games into their 2026 gridiron campaign. Broncos Country is no stranger to slow starts in this respect. However, what we have seen thus far is easily the worst during the Sean Payton era.

Without question, there is a lot of blame to go around. But let’s be brutally honest—quarterback Bo Nix is not playing well at all. There has been no third-year jump from the former first-round pick. In fact, it’s been an abysmal third year slump. All things considered, the Broncos are quite lucky to be 3-2 given his poor play to date.

After their victory over the Chargers, Head Coach Sean Payton expressed confidence with Nix and hopes to see him ‘rip it’ in the weeks to come. But here is the kicker, the Seahawks have one of the best defenses in the NFL. They’ve already forced 11 turnovers on the season. Moreover, they haven’t let an opposing quarterback throw for more than 200 yards on them thus far.

This is arguably the toughest matchup for Nix and the offense yet. Seattle has an elite pass defense. Regardless, that can’t be an excuse for poor play. He needs to step up in the pocket and deliver throws. No more bailing out of clean pockets when there is good enough protection. It’s time for him to start figuring things out.

Star wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba’s impact has to be kept to a minimum

First things first. I came away impressed with how Jahdae Barron and Kris Abrams-Draine performed against the Chargers. Los Angeles was missing their top trio of receivers which can’t be ignored. Even so, I felt the two cornerbacks performed admirably with Denver’s top boundary duo of Patrick Surtain II and Riley Moss sidelined.

Even so, this is one matchup Broncos Country will wish they had Surtain in the starting lineup. Why? Because Jaxon Smith-Njigba is one of the best receivers in the NFL—a premier playmaker who can do it all.

Smith-Njigba is coming off an incredible 2025 campaign. His performance and production were elite. The fourth-year pro led the NFL with 1,793 receiving yards on 119 catches with 10 touchdowns. That was good enough to earn him first-team All-Pro honors, his second Pro-Bowl accolade, as well as the NFL’s Offensive Player of the Year award.

It’s not going to be easy, but Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph has to come up with a game plan that limits the star wide receiver’s impact on the game. That will be quite the challenge with a banged-up secondary that will likely be without star safety Talanoa Hufanga who suffered an ankle injury late in the game versus the Chargers.

Razor thin margins: The Broncos have to win the turnover battle

One of the best developments for the Broncos this season is their defense being able to take the ball away from opponents. They have forced seven turnovers on defense through five games. In addition, they’ve came up in the clutch along with several additional fourth down stops.

In order to secure a primetime victory on Thursday Night Football, the Broncos will need their defense to continue doing that. Winning the turnover battle, especially with Seattle’s defense being elite at forcing them, is an absolute must.

The past three games, quarterback Sam Darnold has made his fair share of plays through the air. Though he has also made a lot of boneheaded mistakes with five interceptions during that time span. Denver’s pass rush came alive late in the game against the Chargers, but it’s important to keep in mind they were starting four rookies in their offensive trenches.

Seattle’s offensive line isn’t perfect, but it’s a lot better than what Denver faced on Sunday. Putting pressure on Darnold to force him to make some mistakes will be huge. Hopefully, the Broncos’ defensive front seven can keep their momentum going and come up with a few big plays that help turn the tide in Denver’s favor in primetime.

item.title: The Hot Read: The Eagles’ bubble is about to burst
item.description: The Philadelphia Eagles are a disaster that everyone sees coming.
item.content:encoded:
When a disaster occurs, there are usually signs long in advance. The 2008 financial crisis, for example. Mortgage lenders got messy and reckless with their money, giving loans to people who had no business receiving them and no way to afford them. But hey, the housing market is in great shape. If those people can’t afford their homes, they can just sell them to people who can at a profit. What could go wrong?!

Oh, housing prices inflated and inflated, creating a bubble that was bound to burst. Then Wall-Street got involved, high-risk loans were sold off to investors, and housing prices tanked – the bubble burst. With the high foreclosure rate now directly intertwined with the economy, the entire country faced a massive recession and millions of people lost their homes. It was easy to see the disaster coming, both in real time and now with the benefit of hindsight.

The same can be said for the 2026 Philadelphia Eagles.

After losing their third consecutive game in unthinkable fashion, the Eagles sit at 2-3 with a long list of injuries, and an even longer list of issues without even as much of a hint of potential solutions.

Future Hall of Fame right tackle Lane Johnson abruptly retired last week, citing his mental health as a large reason why. This came after the Eagles lost to the Los Angeles Rams after holding a 20-10 lead in the fourth quarter – the same game in which they lost Saquon Barkley to a hamstring injury, on top of already being without wide receiver DeVonta Smith due to his own hamstring injury. After Johnson retired, the Eagles traded Pro Bowl center Cam Jurgens to the Baltimore Ravens, receiving a 2028 second-round pick and a 2027 fifth-round pick in return.

And after losing two Pro Bowl offensive linemen, and playing without their two best skill position players, the Eagles trudged their way to just 232 yards of offense against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London, yet still kicked the go-ahead field goal with eight seconds remaining. But somehow, they would find a way to choke away their 17-16 lead, allowing Ameer Abdullah to return the kickoff to their 39 yard-line, setting up a 57 yard field-goal from Cam Little to walk it off for the Jaguars.

Like 2008, though, this crash didn’t just stem out of nowhere. This dates back to the 2025 season. After defeating the Kansas City Chiefs in Super Bowl LIX, things went downhill. Star wide receiver A.J. Brown wasn’t getting the ball, and made it a near weekly occurrence to voice his frustrations, whether it be on social media or through the Eagles media. It was an awkward tension that hung in the air, regardless of a win or loss. After an exhausting season that was spent talking more about what happened on Monday-Saturday than the actual games that were played, Philadelphia was mercifully put away by a depleted San Francisco 49ers team 23-19 in the wild card round. It marked the end of a season where the Eagles, despite all of their talent, finished 23rd in success rate and 19th in scoring.

It also marked the end of A.J. Brown’s career in an Eagles uniform, as he was traded to the New England Patriots. And thus began the reconstruction of Philadelphia’s receiving corps. Smith was elevated to the No. 1 role, which he has shown he is more than capable of handling. The Eagles then drafted USC standout receiver Makai Lemon, and pieced together the rest of the room by signing Hollywood Brown and trading for Dontayvion Wicks. On paper, the unit is solid. In practice, it has been a disaster.

Smith has dealt with the aforementioned hamstring injury, which has kept him out of two games. Lemon is averaging just 7.2 yards per catch, and Hurts is averaging less than 190 yards passing. Through five weeks, the Eagles’ offense ranks 30th in EPA per play and 30th in passing success rate. They also can’t put points on the board, ranking 29th in scoring.

Which leads us to the bubble. The bubble that will inevitably pop. Jalen Hurts’ contract is becoming worse by the day. He ranks 31st in EPA per play (min. 25 dropbacks), and carries a dead cap hit of $101 million in 2027. His contract’s total value is the seventh-highest among quarterbacks, and his play is much closer to reflecting that of the 27th best quarterback in the league.

In terms of 2026, they have to play with 52 players on the roster after Johnson’s retirement due to him carrying over $63 million in dead cap for this season.

For the future, there is a lot of money tied up in older players. Saquon Barkley is going to be 31 and his play is already on the decline – he carries a cap hit of over $13 million and a dead cap north of $28 million in 2027. Zack Baun will be 32 – $11.8 million cap hit, $22.2 million dead cap hit. Jonathan Greenard will be 31 and currently has zero sacks – $11.1 million cap hit, $43.5 million dead cap hit. The iceberg is in sight, and the ship has no way to change course.

With each loss and offensive inefficiency, the bubble inflates that much more, and the collateral of the burst could include head coach Nick Sirianni. If there is anything the Eagles have shown, it’s that no one, not even a Super Bowl-winning head coach, is safe if results yield.

That was the cold open. This is the Hot Read.

Three and out

The Bills and Rams have real problems

The Buffalo Bills and Los Angeles Rams gave us an instant classic on Monday night, with the two teams combining for seven lead changes, 35 fourth-quarter points, two fumbles, one blocked field goal, and one game-winner from Tyler Bass to give the Bills a huge road win (Josh Allen’s first in OT) to get them to 4-1. Despite the win, though, this isn’t a Bills team with a sustainable style of winning.

Through five games, Buffalo has surrendered at least 30 points three times, and gave up 29 last week to the New England Patriots. Their 166 points given up are the most in the NFL, and opposing offenses have picked apart their secondary at will. They’ve allowed the second-most passing yards and second-most touchdown passes in the league. This completely inadequate play on defense makes the margin for error next to zero for Josh Allen and the offense. And while the Bills’ offense has been good, ranking first in the league in EPA per play and points per game, we’ve seen this movie before. Come playoff time, their defense will cost them, once again.

On the other side, the Rams have a roster full of future Hall of Famers, and yet they sit at 2-3. One game got away and was stolen from them on a pass interference call that the NFL said shouldn’t have been called, they opened the season in Australia where the ball was kicked off about 9 minutes after they arrived, and special teams woes from a season ago have carried over into 2026. Harrison Mevis missed a pair of kicks that would have sealed a win over Buffalo, and the opening kickoff was nearly returned for a touchdown by Ray Davis and set up a Bills field goal. Special teams cost the Rams last year in a loss to the Seattle Seahawks, which ultimately cost them the No. 1 seed. It could cost them much more than that in 2026.

While both the Bills and Rams are popular picks to represent their respective conferences in the Super Bowl, they both have glaring issues that, if left uncorrected, will have both spending Valentine’s Day with their wives instead of facing each other in a rematch for all the marbles.

The Broncos offense still stinks

It was only a matter of time before Sean Payton took back play-calling duties for the Broncos, and eagle-eyed readers will remember I predicted that to happen in my 61 Predictions piece back in July. I said it would happen in Week 9, and he beat me by a month.

On the surface, it makes sense for Payton to take over as the play-caller. Many argued he shouldn’t have given it up to begin with, and with him taking back the reins, the offense would improve. Except it didn’t. Denver put up just 224 yards of offense, with Bo Nix going 16-of-27 for just 123 yards. If you look at Nix’s passing charts from Week 4 and Week 5, they look virtually identical – a ton of passes behind, at, or just beyond the line of scrimmage with very few shots downfield and the middle of the field completely vacant.

The play-caller may have changed, but one thing remains very evident that we’ve touched on all season – this is not a coaching staff that believes in its quarterback. And in case you needed a deeper look at how poor Nix has played, he’s 29th in EPA per play (one spot behind Deshaun Watson), 33rd in success rate (0.1 percent higher than Cam Ward), and his average depth of target is just 5.81 yards downfield, good for 39th in the NFL. This isn’t a franchise quarterback, and the Broncos know it. Now they get to take that offense on the road to Seattle on a short week – Godspeed.

The Packers bring the Bears down to Earth

The first four weeks of the season were rough for the Packers. They allowed 22 fourth-quarter points in Week 1 to lose to the Vikings, had to put together a first of its kind comeback against the Jets, got boat-raced in their home opener against the Falcons, and barely beat the Buccaneers sans Baker Mayfield. But in Week 5 against their arch rival Chicago Bears, they came to life. Jordan Love connected on four passes that were good for 40+ yards, finishing the day with 367 yards and two long touchdowns to Christian Watson. Defensively, the Packers picked off Tyson Bagent and Case Keenum three times en route to a 31-7 blowout win.

In finally seeing their offense take off, the Packers also sent Ben Johnson and the Bears back down to Earth, and maybe now we can cool it a bit on treating Ben Johnson as if he single-handedly found the cure for cancer. A week after putting up just under 500 yards, the Packers’ defense limited Chicago to 268. Cracks in the defense certainly peeked through, as well, with the aforementioned deep passing success of Love. They are currently still a top 15 unit in terms of success rate, but the explosive plays against the secondary were what many worried about with Chicago’s defense entering the season, and this is now something to monitor.

So after the Bears were treated like the youngest child in a family of four for the first month of the year while the Packers were portrayed as the uncle you don’t want to invite to Thanksgiving but you do anyway to be nice, and then he inevitably drinks one too many and begins sharing his thoughts on the southern border, both are 3-2 – the NFL has a funny way of doing that.

Buy or sell

Buy: The Commanders need to fire Dan Quinn

Maybe it’s an extreme reaction, but when this much incompetence is put on display for a team that is now 1-3-1, what more do you need? I’m sure you’ve seen it by now. The Commanders had the ball in field foal range with 40 seconds left in overtime with no timeouts. And with all the urgency of a divorced father making an alimony payment, the Commanders let roughly 20 second tick off the clock before Jayden Daniels took the snap and dove forward. They couldn’t get back to spike the ball in time, and the game ended in a 27-27 tie as Dan Quinn spiked his headset with the fury of a thousand lame duck head coaches. Less than two years after coaching in the NFC Championship Game, Quinn has one of the hottest seats in the sport. The Commanders are 6-15-1 since getting to within a game of the Super Bowl, and their defense – Quinn’s side of the ball – is 31st in EPA per play in that span. The writing is on the wall in Washington, and I’d bet Anthony Lynn serves as the team’s interim head coach before season’s end.

Sell: The Cleveland Browns

It was only a matter of time before the other shoe dropped with the Browns. Even after a 3-1 start that saw them holding the AFC North lead after four weeks, this team always felt like it had a hard ceiling due to its quarterback and lack of high-end veteran talent. That was all proven correct against the New York Jets, who defeated the Browns in a game that featured rain showers from beginning to end. Despite only having 198 yards of total offense, it looked as if the Browns would steal a win after a Deshaun Watson touchdown pass to Denzel Boston with 6:15 to play. Unfortunately for Cleveland, a bad snap on a late punt was recovered by the Jets at the Browns’ 23 yard-line. Braelon Allen ran it in, and the Jets took a 17-12 lead that they’d never give back. Now at 3-2, they face the Ravens and Steelers in two of their next three games.

Buy: The Patriots have found their groove

After a horrid start to the year, the New England Patriots have found their mojo. New England started 1-2, and their MVP candidate quarterback looked lost in the midst of it. Through the first three weeks of the season, Drake Maye threw one touchdown to six interceptions. Over his last two games, that ratio went to seven touchdowns and one interception.

Four of those scores came against the Las Vegas Raiders in a dominant 45-17 win that also saw Maye throw for 374 yards. Despite starting off the year scoring just 19 points in their first three games, New England ranks first in EPA per play in the last two weeks and is averaging 37 points per game in that span.

Sell: Jim Harbaugh as the Chargers head coach in 2027

The Chargers are a McRib presenting to be a Michelin star quality meal. Everyone once again drank their Kool-Aid this offseason – if only they had listened to me. The offense was supposed to transcend the NFL after hiring Mike McDaniel, and that offense currently ranks dead last in EPA per play. Not the Titans, not the Dolphins – the Chargers. Justin Herbert is also fundamentally broke, throwing five touchdowns to seven interceptions while leading a unit that ranks 30th in scoring. Harbaugh was brought in to take the Chargers to the next level, and he has yet to win a playoff game since being hired. This is a team that will tear everything down going into 2027, and that includes the head coach, and maybe even the quarterback.

One play that changed everything

I had a nice little soliloquy typed up about Kim Kinchens’ tackle on Khalil Shakir in overtime saving the day for the Rams, as it led to Nate Landman’s forced fumble on James Cook that gave the Rams the ball back. Instead, the play that changed everything goes to Buffalo Bills edge rusher Greg Rousseau, who has been on a tear to begin this campaign. Harrison Mevis trotted out to kick the game-winning field goal to sent the Rams to 3-2, but Rousseau broke through and got a paw on the kick, forcing it to land short and give the ball back to Josh Allen and the Bills offense. Allen ran for 32 yards on the ensuing drive and set up Tyler Bass for his own attempt to win the game, which he did, to send Buffalo to 4-1 in an absolute thriller.

Prediction to track

  • Week 1: Steelers will trade Joey Porter Jr: Correct
  • Week 2: Rams will beat Broncos handedly: Incorrect
  • Week 3: Lions will blowout Panthers: Incorrect
  • Week 4: Marvin Harrison Jr and Brian Thomas Jr will be traded: Half correct

Well, I said Marvin Harrison and Brian Thomas would both be traded before the deadline, and Harrison has officially been shipped to Houston. After a game in London that featured no catches, I won’t be shocked if news of a Thomas trade happens sooner than later for a receiver-needy team.

This week, I’ll say that Jordan Love will have another explosive game agains the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday night, where he will throw for 321 yards and three touchdowns as Green Bay defeats Dallas 33-27.

item.title: Fantasy Football Film Review: 5 things that stood out to Hayden Winks from Week 5
item.description: Fantasy football analyst Hayden Winks enters the Week 5 film room.
item.content:encoded:
Fantasy football is inundated with stats and charts (guilty!), but the more context the film provides, the more reliable the data gets. That's why we have a 2.5-hour show called Stats vs. Film every Tuesday at 6 p.m. EST. That show is live — join us in the chat!

This (experimental) weekly column will look at some of the biggest storylines I picked up by grinding the film. 

Ashton Jeanty is not playing fast enough

His ankle and foot injury partially explains this, but this was Jeanty's primary problem as a rookie, too. Jeanty's particular issue is quickly changing direction and bursting through the hole or away from a space defender. This isn't overly surprising, as it's uncommon for the elite RB prospects to skip NFL Combine testing, and Jeanty did just that.

pic.twitter.com/fxdOUKHoqL

— WinksTape (@WinksTape) October 12, 2026

Compared to the elite RBs, Jeanty's processing is forgettable. The play above is an example of not seeing things well. We have an inside zone run, where the C is going to climb to the LB after engaging with the DT. Jeanty doesn't trust it, stutters his feet and misses a potential window to hit the hole. 

pic.twitter.com/oWo2wKPKdZ

— WinksTape (@WinksTape) October 12, 2026

This is another missed read, this time on a power run. Jeanty should be trailing his pulling guard and waiting for him to block the LB. Instead, Jeanty is impatient and bounces it toward Brock Bowers, who lost his matchup. There is a hole up in the middle if he finds it. On man and power runs this year, Jeanty is averaging 3.0 yards per carry. 

Some of this absolutely falls on the Raiders OL not getting enough push on their individual blocks. The lack of yards before contact (0.6) this season is not dissimilar to what happened last year. Unfortunately, the more we learn about yards before contact, the more we learn that the RB has more say in it than originally given credit for.

Here are the bottom 10 RBs in yards before contact this season, and it's not a coincidence that they are the slowest RBs in the NFL:

My last note on Jeanty is as a receiver. He's very capable on option routes and the occasional downfield route, but he's simply dropped too many passes, particularly over the middle on fast balls from Kirk Cousins. The Raiders might be trying to evaluate exactly how they can use him in the pass game because his protection has included multiple pretty fatal reps. Dylan Laube was playing a lot more than usual last week, limiting Jeanty to 53% snaps in the first half. Some of that is the injury, but some of that is because he's not an elite bellcow back.

Jeremiyah Love looked healthier than his box score

Following a new right ankle sprain in Week 4, Love managed to get in a full practice heading into Sunday. He started, played in the 2-minute drill and started the second half before being shelved in a dead fourth quarter. He totally busted in the box score, but how did he look?

His film looked healthy! 

weeeeeeee

(Jeremiyah Love looked healthy to me) pic.twitter.com/HFr5V2PLpP

— Hayden Winks (@HaydenWinks) October 12, 2026

There was a wild jump over a blocker, many quick cuts and enough reps of him getting up to speed to believe he can be productive if the Cardinals allow it. Where the tape was concerning was across the OL. They don't have starting LT Parris Johnson Jr. for the rest of the year, and the rest of the OL has been problematic all season. There simply wasn't a lot of room to run in Week 5 against the Lions.

Love was on the field for the goal-line play-action rep before garbage time, so there might be a little more value in this role than what we saw last week in real garbage time. The comments around Love's happiness and health are concerning, but the Cardinals are going to get real desperate here. 

Beyond his health, the consistent thing on his film is he's been a little too jumpy/dancy. He's a very explosive player who can jump around defenders and find hidden holes, but there are other times where he's jumping around to nowhere. Finding that balance is what turns the good starters into the great ones. 

Matthew Golden is extremely legit

Small sample noise can lead us astray, but Golden is just very good. It's as simple as that. There will be an occasional drop or miscommunication with Jordan Love given his experience, but Golden moves like the top downfield receivers in the NFL. His explosiveness at the line is obvious; he can maintain separation downfield, and he has springs at the catch point.

All of that manifested on this man-coverage rep against CB1 Jaylon Johnson:

Matthew Golden is so so fast.

Like how he ripped the ball away after catching it, too. pic.twitter.com/ic8261RdtZ

— Hayden Winks (@HaydenWinks) October 12, 2026

You'll notice Jordan Love saw the matchup after peaking to Golden's side, checked out of the run and then launched it to him with perfect placement. Golden had an extremely similar rep up the seam, too.

Beyond this rep, Golden is adding multiple quick-hitting reps, like screens, slants, hitches and scramble-drill wins, so his floor is higher than others with this downfield ability. He's on pace for 80 receptions and 1,350 yards right now. If Love is going to have as much time in the pocket as he did last year after the Packers began moving around their starting offensive linemen, then this team can rip explosives with the best of them.

Love had six completions for 252 yards on passes over 20 air yards, both a single-game high this season. He also had a phantom OPI called back that would've made his stat 7-302-2.

Germie Bernard has some bad, some good

Bernard is the consensus top waiver wire add of the week. The role is undeniable with Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) on injured reserve, and Roman Wilson (finger) expected to be out multiple weeks. Bernard ran a route on 36 of 38 Week 5 dropbacks. That's enough to be an auto top-50 fantasy WR, but the question is, can he be a bye-week starter in fantasy?

In Week 2, Bernard had a bubble screen clank off his chest for a horrid interception, one that required Aaron Rodgers himself to make the tackle. I'm sure Rodgers loved that. 

A couple of very rookie mistakes mixed in, but the Steelers are going to live with them for the next few weeks. He played 36-of-38 routes, between slot and flanker. pic.twitter.com/dScKieCKxB

— Hayden Winks (@HaydenWinks) October 12, 2026

This week, Bernard had two other drops. Bernard's toughest drop began by not knowing the play. Once again as the flanker, Bernard began blocking for a run play and realized he had a route to run. He cut inside, just where Jaylen Warren was expected to be as the checkdown. Bernard sat right in front of Warren, then dropped it. That's what it's like playing as a rookie in a dense Rodgers offense. 

His other one was the flanker in a trips set, running a seam ball against zone coverage after Rodgers drew an edge offside. While turning around, Bernard dropped a perfect pass that would've gone for an explosive. Drops happen, so this wasn't so bad.

The next one, well …

The good of Germie Bernard in Week 5. Aaron Rodgers likes him in these tight spaces and on in-cut routes. He's a tough player with nice size, so this role suits him well.

Season-high 12.0 expected points. pic.twitter.com/iPVib2gcm4

— Hayden Winks (@HaydenWinks) October 12, 2026

The Steelers seem willing to live with the mistakes, and Rodgers has even spent pre-production time talking up his second-round rookie. I loved Bernard's versatility and toughness on his Alabama tape, so I do hope he can round out his game immediately. Bernard's positive plays in Week 5 reflected those traits. He had two slant wins in traffic, then two big-boy dig routes for chunk gains. Rodgers likes to throw these underneath passes into tight windows, and Bernard has the size and willingness to be targeted here.

Rapid-Fire Notes

— Jaylen Warren is a star. There's no competition between him and Rico Dowdle. Don't let anyone tell you otherwise.

This Jaylen Warren run went for 50 pic.twitter.com/4Pms4Ntw7b

— Hayden Winks (@HaydenWinks) October 12, 2026

— Tyler Shough (left hand) had to hand the ball off only with his right hand. I wouldn't be surprised if his non-throwing hand is broken right now. Speaking of broken, the Saints have the worst RB and TE blocking rooms in the NFL. That's really what broke the Saints versus Brian Flores.

— Many of Kyler Murray's biggest plays were a bit out of structure. His speed on scrambles was excellent and very valuable. There were also chunk passing gains in the scramble drill, and his big touchdown pass to Justin Jefferson was after he got bumped off his route. Even while he learns the feel of this new downfield offense, Murray's play-making is a fun backup plan. The Vikings are heading on bye now, and they could absolutely use it with their injuries.

— Parker Washington is excellent. His physicality and ball skills have been evident since late last year. That showed up again when he peaked around the much-bigger Riq Woolen before extending his other hand for a one-handed TD. What I didn't realize was how fast he is in a straight line. His long, leaking TD showcased burst that is reminiscent of the top slot/flanker types, like Steve Smith Sr. Washington is going to get the biggest bag at any moment. 

— Makai Lemon just might not be quick enough to be a difference-maker. A quick slant covered by Travis Hunter was pretty glaring in terms of movement skills and length. There was another screen called for him that went incomplete because he initially went out to block. This isn't the first time that's happened this year, so don't be surprised if his snaps stagnate or reduce with Darius Cooper playing better and offering more in the run game. Lemon is droppable.

— The Eagles had another 10 unblocked pressures (bad), but they attacked it differently this time around. They went empty to simplify things and often threw it downfield. Those went incomplete this time, but this was a better plan for Jalen Hurts when teams are blitzing. It's evident that they don't trust their fourth- and fifth-string RBs in protection, nor should they. The other thing with the new-look Eagles offense is a pivot away from the Tush Push. Neither of their 1-yard-to-go plays were pushes, and their new C (who had some bad snaps) and extremely undersized new LG (who had five pressures allowed) aren't equipped to run it. That really hurts Hurts' fantasy value.

— Tyler Warren is being utilized more downfield without Alec Pierce. In 17 games with Pierce, his aDOT is just 4.5 yards downfield. In seven games without Pierce involved, Warren's aDOT is up to 6.5 yards. Last week's 9.9 aDOT was the second highest of his career. He had a pair of wheel routes up the sideline, then more breaking routes in the 8-15 yard range. Those will be helpful for the next few weeks. A bonus FB dive at the goal line for a score is also helpful.

item.content:encoded:
The Eagles won't issue their injury designations for Week 6 until Friday, but defensive coordinator Vic Fangio all but ruled one member of the defense out on Tuesday.

Linebacker Jalyx Hunt left last Sunday's loss to the Jaguars with knee and ankle injuries. Fangio said at his weekly press conference, via multiple reporters, that it would be "miraculous" if Hunt is able to play against the Panthers in Week 6.

Hunt had three tackles and a pass defensed against Jacksonville. He has 15 tackles, a tackle for loss and four quarterback hits on the season.

The Eagles played without Jonathan Greenard in Week 5 due to an ankle injury, so they were down to Nolan Smith, Arnold Ebiketie, and A.J. Epenesa on the edge after Hunt's injury.

The Pittsburgh Steelers are dealing with the injury bug. Specifically, the wide receiver room has been hit big time with the short-term IR trip for Michael Pittman Jr. and the news of a potential multi-week absence for Roman Wilson, who was primed to take on a bigger role with Pittman Jr.’s injury. item.title: NFL power rankings: Nick’s picks for how teams stack up before Week 6
item.description: Nick’s Power Rankings heading into Week 6
item.content:encoded:
No. 1 — San Francisco 49ers (5-0) | SAME

The 49ers keep rolling after an impressive road win in Seattle. Mike Evans went OFF, catching seven passes for 113 yards and a touchdown while battling through rib injuries. His addition has provided the Kyle Shanahan offense with a much-needed outside threat who is playing unreal late in his career. The defense forced four turnovers, as the 49ers continue to dominate.

No. 2 —Buffalo Bills (4-1) | SAME

The New England Patriots came to play! The Bills’ defense surrendered 405 yards in the game, but a late Josh Allen interception, followed by a 12-yard Hunter Henry catch on third-and-10, secured the victory for New England. The 49ers jump the Bills here, but Buffalo is still a top-three team in the NFL.

No. 3 — Kansas City Chiefs (4-0) | 📉 1 spot

The Chiefs were on their BYE, but still have persistent questions about their weapons on offense after the injury to Tyquon Thornton last week. Still, they’re finding ways to win, have Patrick Mahomes, and Steve Spagnuolo’s defense is playing well.

No. 4 — Minnesota Vikings (5-0) | (6th) 📈 1 spot

The Vikings defense continues to be elite. They held the Saints to 142 yards and Tyler Shough to 96 passing yards. Aaron Jones rushed for 113 yards and a touchdown on 25 carries, while Kyler Murray threw for 211 yards with a dime to Justin Jefferson. The Vikings offense is getting by, but the defense has carried them to an undefeated record through five weeks.

No. 5 — Los Angeles Rams (2-3) | SAME

The Rams lost a heartbreaker in overtime, 37-34. Josh Allen did Josh Allen things at the end of the game. Both Allen and James Cook rushed for over 100 yards in the game. Matt Stafford threw for 383 yards and three touchdowns, while Puka Nacua caught 17 balls for 138 yards. Rams have three losses, but they’re still a top team in the NFL.

No. 6 — Seattle Seahawks (3-2) | (3rd) 📉 3 spots

Seattle turned the football over four times against the 49ers, who were all over Sam Darnold. Seattle could not stop Mike Evans. Sure, Seattle has two losses, but they’re still a top team in the league.

No. 7 — Jacksonville Jaguars (4-1) | (8th) 📈 1 spots

Cam Little’s last-second field goal let Jacksonville steal a win in London, where they’ll play the Texans next week. Parker Washington played very well in the win and was the solution for Liam Coen’s offense against an Eagles offense that has no identity.

No. 8 —Baltimore Ravens (4-1) | (9th) 📈 1 spot

Baltimore closed out a tight game with a nice comeback win over the Atlanta Falcons. Tyler Huntley did what he had to in the 30-23 victory. Baltimore should be receiving Lamar Jackson back either this week or the next.

No. 9 — New England Patriots (3-2) | (14th) 📈 5 spots

New England is back?! The Patriots destroyed the Las Vegas Raiders at home, 45-17, which likely made Josh McDaniels smile. Drake Maye threw for 374 yards in the win. The Patriots defense SHUT down the Raiders’ rushing attack and has stabilized over the past two weeks.

No. 10 — Chicago Bears (3-2) | (7th) 📉 3 spots

The Bears were embarrassed by the Green Bay Packers, 31-7. It was bad; Tyson Bagent couldn’t do much offensively, but it was the Chicago defense that could NOT stop Jordan Love and the Packers’ passing offense. Case Keenum moved the offense a bit, but it wasn’t enough. A game to forget for the Bears, but it sets up well for the rematch between Matt LaFleur and Ben Johnson in Week 16.

No. 11 — Cincinnati Bengals (3-2) | (12th) 📈 1 spot

The Bengals escaped Miami with a 31-24 win. Miami scored two fourth-quarter touchdowns, which made the game look more respectable, but it was Joe Burrow who threw four touchdowns, despite just 190 total yards on 23 completions. Miami did, however, gain 331 total yards and turned the football over three times, while rushing for 217 total yards, 74 of which were by quarterback Malik Willis.

No. 12— Detroit Lions (3-2) | (16th) 📈4 spots

Detroit dropped 45 on the Cardinals in the desert, beating Arizona 45-21. Jahmyr Gibbs rushed for 151 yards on 25 carries and two touchdowns, and the Lions offense looked like what we’re used to seeing. Jared Goff added three passing touchdowns.

No. 13 — Carolina Panthers (2-2) | (15th) 📈 1 spot

Carolina was on a BYE, but moved up one spot in the rankings!

No. 14 — Pittsburgh Steelers (3-2) | (20th) 📈 6 spots

The Pittsburgh Steelers established the run well with Jaylen Warren, who had 101 yards on 15 carries with a touchdown. Aaron Rodgers threw for 235 yards and three touchdowns in the Steelers’ 34-22 win against the Colts.

No. 15 — Denver Broncos (3-2) | (13th ) 📉 2 spots

The Broncos won a divisional matchup on the road against the Los Angeles Chargers, but their offense still doesn’t look right under Sean Payton. Their defense is a top unit in the league, but Bo Nix and the offense have struggled. Denver had 224 total yards, with Nix throwing for just 123 yards. Still, a win is a win.

No. 16 — Las Vegas Raiders (3-2) | (11th) 📉 5 spots

The Raiders were embarrassed by the Patriots and not much went right for Kirk Cousins and Klint Kubiak. We did see, however, Fernando Mendoza, who went 6 of 8 for 48 yards in garbage time. Las Vegas did nothing on the ground against this Patriots front; Asthon Jeanty had 27 yards on 10 carries.

No. 17 — Green Bay Packers (3-2) | (26th) 📈 9 spots

The Packers have three wins despite this season going TERRIBLY so far. But, WOW, did the Packers’ offense turn on against the Bears’ defense: a 31-7 win where Jordan Love threw for 367 yards and two touchdowns. MarShawn Lynch rushed for a pair of touchdowns as well, while only averaging 3.1 yards per carry.

No. 18 — New York Giants (3-1-1) | 📈 1 spot

The Giants tied the Washington Commanders, 27-27, and they had the win in their hands but missed a field goal and fumbled it away; but the Commanders also did not want to win the football game, which led to one of the wilder endings I’ve ever covered. The Giants may look to spread things out and operate out of the shotgun with Jameis Winston, for it’s obvious he’s more comfortable letting it sling, rather than operating a heavy play action passing attack that can’t run the ball anyway.

No. 19 — Atlanta Falcons (2-3) | (17th) 📉 2 spots

Atlanta lost in overtime at home to a backup quarterback — not ideal! Still, the Ravens are a well-coached team, and perhaps the game ends differently if Tua Tagovailoa wasn’t forced into action. Michael Penix Jr. perhaps doesn’t throw the game-sealing interception. Still, Atlanta lost the game, but they’re better than their 2-3 record would suggest.

No. 20 — Dallas Cowboys (2-3) | (10th) 📉 10 spots

Dallas was beaten by a backup quarterback on Thursday Night Football. The Buccaneers dominated for much of the game, despite a late push by Dak Prescott. The final score was 24-16; Christian Parker’s defense has been an abject disaster, as Bucky Irving rumbled for 165 yards and a touchdown on the ground.

No. 21 — Houston Texans (1-4) | (23rd) 📈 2 spots

The Texans beat up on the Tennessee Titans, 26-3. C.J. Stroud threw for 261 yards and a touchdown, but the Texans lost David Montgomery to an injury in the game. I don’t like having the Texans this high, but, like the Falcons, they’ve underperformed and failed to finish close games against solid opponents earlier in the season.

No. 22 — Cleveland Browns (3-2) | (18th) 📉 4 spots

The Cleveland Browns fell to the Jets, 17-12, at MetLife Stadium. Braelon Allen ran for 116 yards and a touchdown in the game, as Garrett Wilson caught seven passes for 104 yards with a score against the Browns, who could not get much going on offense.

No. 23 — Philadelphia Eagles (2-3) | (22nd) 📉 1 spot

The Eagles are a mess offensively, as they lost in a last-second field goal against the Jacksonville Jaguars. Even though the Eagles are beat up on the offensive line, they’re trading Pro Bowl offensive linemen. Still, their defense is a solid unit, but the team is lost right now.

No. 24 — Indianapolis Colts (2-3) | (21st) 📉 3 spots

Daniel Jones threw for 267 yards against Pittsburgh, but the Colts did little on the ground, as the Steelers rolled to a 34-22 win. Jonathan Taylor averaged just three yards per carry. Indianapolis went 4 of 15 on third down, and the Colts turned the football over on downs twice in the fourth quarter.

No. 25 — Washington Commanders (1-3-1) | (24th) 📉 1 spot

Washington was a disaster in that end-of-game situation. Getting Jayden Daniels back is huge for Washington, but the Giants’ defense shut down the offense —for the most part. Daniels, though, has to do a better job at the end of the game to secure that victory.

No. 26 — New York Jets (2-3) (28th) 📈 2 spots

The Jets offense was much better in their Week 5 win against the Cleveland Browns. They won 17-12, scoring 10 points in the fourth quarter to seal the victory. New York had 276 yards on offense on 65 plays, up from 32 last week.

No. 27 — New Orleans Saints (1-3) (25th) 📉 1 spot

The Saints couldn’t do anything against the Vikings at home. Brian Flores will do that.

No. 28 — Tampa Bay Buccaneers (1-4) | 📈 3 spots

The Buccaneers pulled off an upset on Thursday Night Football as they await Baker Mayfield’s return. The Buccaneers’ defense stifled the Dallas offense. The Buccaneers have an uphill battle, but the NFC South is still open.

No. 29 — Arizona Cardinals (1-3) | (27th) 📉 2 spots

Arizona surrendered 45 points to the Detroit Lions. They couldn’t stop Gibbs and did not do much offensively to challenge the Lions, although Trey McBride had a WILD touchdown grab.

No. 30 — Los Angeles Chargers (0-5) | (29th) 📉 1 spot

The Chargers remain winless. Their offense is an absolute mess, and Justin Herbert looked lost against the Broncos. He was sacked five times; neither offense played well in the game, but the Chargers are the league’s biggest disappointments through five weeks.

No. 31 — Miami Dolphins (0-5) | (32d) 📈 1 spot

Miami made the score against the Bengals look respectable, but Cincinnati controlled the game. Still, this is — at least — the second consecutive game where the Dolphins kept it…interesting. Ollie Gordon had another solid outing too.

No. 32 — Tennessee Titans (0-) 5| (31st) 📉1 spot

The Texans dismantled Tennessee, and the team remains winless and has struggled offensively.

item.title: Panthers designate RB Trevor Etienne for return, put DT Cam Jackson on IR
