item.title: Patriots RB TreVeyon Henderson will reportedly miss 'multiple' weeks with high ankle sprain
item.description: Henderson was injured after being tackles following a run in the second quarter.
item.content:encoded:
The New England Patriots are expected to be without running back TreVeyon Henderson for some time after he suffered a high ankle sprain during Sunday's win over the Las Vegas Raiders.

According to ESPN's Adam Schefter, Henderson, who ran for 22 yards on four carries and made one reception for 16 yards, could miss "multiple" weeks, but will not require surgery to repair the ankle.

Henderson suffered the injury following an 11-yard run early in the second quarter. He came up limping and was eventually ruled out for the rest of the game midway through the third quarter.

Henderson wasn't the only Patriot to go down in Week 5. Left tackle Will Campbell suffered a knee sprain two plays before Henderson was injured. He was also ruled out of the game in the third quarter and his injury is to the same knee where he tore his MCL last season.

NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported on Sunday night that Campbell is also expected to miss time, but an exact timeframe has not been announced.

"We hate to see it," said Patriots running back Rhamondre Stevenson, who ran for 64 yards and a touchdown in the 45-17 win. "We want everybody on this football team to be available and help us win. But the game of football, the NFL, that's kind of going to come.

"This year has been a lot more than we would want, but it's kind of 'next-man-up' mentality. It speaks volumes to the people, practice squad [players], those who don't get many opportunities, how locked in they come to work every day. I'm proud of them. We have to keep it going until we get guys back."

The 3-2 Patriots will host the New York Jets on Sunday night before visiting the Chicago Bears on Sunday night in Week 7.

item.description: Throw this one away for the Browns’ offense.
item.content:encoded:
You hate to throw things out the window in terms of judgment of this game, but that’s sort of what I did with respect to the Browns’ offensive performance against the Jets. It was raining all game, and got heavier in the fourth quarter. When the rain was forecast, my expectations turned to a low-scoring game, with the potential for some turnovers. Why, then, would I get extra concerned about the offense because my expectations were met?

Below, we analyze the snap counts and stats on offense for the Cleveland Browns’ Week 5 game against the New York Jets.

Quarterback

  • The Jets were able to sack Deshaun Watson eight times. Between that, the running game not working, and a few penalties, we saw Watson try to push the ball downfield a few times in earlier downs to make up yards. It went against the formula of taking those short, open passes in previous weeks to help get easy, efficient yards.
  • I also thought later in the game that Watson tried to take off a few times in situations where he probably should’ve tried to let something rip, even if it led to an interception. Granted, we didn’t see what the receiving opportunities looked like on those plays, but still. I’m thinking more about the 4th-and-11 sack he took to conclude the game.
  • PFF graded Watson out to a 48.2 on offense.

Running Back

  • I remain down on Quinshon Judkins. I feel like I’m beating a dead horse each week, but when you see all of the team’s impressive rookies, Judkins has fallen to the back of the line. There is nothing about his running style or ability right now that looks special or even starter-worthy. He does not look like the same back from pre-injury a year ago. PFF graded him as the team’s worst offensive player (41.7).
  • What really drove me crazy about Judkins is him going out of bounds to stop the clock with about four minutes to go, right after the defense got the turnover. I know there are other things that contributed to the loss, but I wonder if that created a trickle down effect of needing to throw the ball as opposed to running more clock, which led to the butterfly effect of the bad punt snap and go-ahead touchdown for the Jets.
  • Jaleel McLaughlin received some more snaps this week. Unfortunately, he dropped the one open pass that came his way that could have been a pretty decent-looking gain in the first half.

Wide Receiver

  • Once again, Denzel Boston came up with a big catch, using his speed and size to haul in a go-ahead touchdown catch mid-way through the fourth quarter.
  • KC Concepcion got two early targets, but the second one didn’t count because he was knocked out (penalty negates the target). Even though you have the next-man up mentality, when you consider the timing Watson tries to build with the receivers, and the rain, that certainly could’ve impacted the game.
  • For example, Isaiah Bond got a huge boost in reps this week. In fact, Boston, he, and Jerry Jeudy all had 70%+ of the snaps, so Cleveland went with more three-receiver looks. But Bond had more big-play opportunities come his way. Watson just barely missed a touchdown pass to him, throwing it beyond his reach. And trying to rally late, Watson hit him open over the middle and he dropped it. Despite that, PFF graded Bond out to a 63.7.

Tight End

  • Harold Fannin only had one catch late and was a non-factor in the rainy conditions. He was the Browns’ second-lowest graded player by PFF, grading out to a 43.9.

Offensive Line

  • Tytus Howard was dinged up early in the game, tried to return, and eventually seemed to give way to Dawand Jones. I know Howard hasn’t been the best this season, but Dawand Jones was the team’s lowest-graded lineman (46.9) by a wide margin this week, as Zion Johnson, Spencer Fano, and Elgton Jenkins all graded respectably despite all the sacks we saw.

item.title: Eagles News: The case for punting on the 2026 season
item.description: Philadelphia Eagles news and links for 10/13/26.
item.content:encoded:
Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation!

I happen to agree with BGN alumnus Jimmy Kempski’s assessment of the 2026 Eagles. This team is probably cooked. Sure, they’re not far off from being 4-1. And maybe they even win a bad NFC East. But they just haven’t played very well on the whole, especially relative to other teams. This isn’t their year. And that’s OK! They’ve been on one of the most successful runs, if not THE most, in franchise history. Although it’s certainly disappointing, they’re allowed to have a bad year without it meaning doom and gloom for the franchise moving forward. I’m still pretty optimistic about the Eagles’ long-term future with Jeffrey Lurie and Howie Roseman at the helm. Expecting the Eagles to flat out tank isn’t realistic but the front office should absolutely be making decisions with more than the team’s 2026 outlook in mind. Taking a step back this year could position the Eagles very well in future seasons. It is indeed time for a reset.

Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links …

The Eagles should punt on the 2026 season, trade still-valuable players for future assets – PhillyVoice

We’re only five weeks into the 2026 NFL season, but it is already crystal clear that it is not going to be a special one for the Philadelphia Eagles. More bluntly, if you’re a Birds fan, this season sucks. And, spoiler, it is only going to continue to suck. However, Howie Roseman and the Eagles are in a position to choose their suckage path the rest of the season. One is to try to compete for a division title in the craptastic NFC East, and if successful pretend that anything can happen in the playoffs. The other is to maximize the value on likely soon-to-be outgoing players, and reset the roster for another long-term run. One is to try to compete for a division title in the craptastic NFC East, and if successful pretend that anything can happen in the playoffs. The decision really shouldn’t be all that hard. They should choose the reset.

Seven things Solak thinks entering NFL Week 6: Time for Mendoza? Cowboys issues? – ESPN

I think … neither coach whose team committed end-of-game errors on Sunday will survive the season. […] Sirianni said after the game when asked about the touchback decision: “I didn’t make the right decision, and I lost us that game, and that’s what I said to our guys.” It echoes what he has said about the Eagles’ errant fourth-down decision-making over the past few games — passing on go-worthy fourth downs only to attempt more difficult ones later. The buck stops with him. He’s right, of course. And if the Eagles cannot hang the laurels of playcalling or coach development on Sirianni’s chest; if they can’t call him an elite mediator of disgruntled players; if they can’t expect him to maximize winning chances with fourth-down decisions or clock management … what do they ask of him? What does he bring to a team in transition — a team that’s wondering if it’s finally time to take its medicine and rebuild for a new era of contention?

Eagles vs. Jaguars: 8 winners, 8 losers, 6 IDKs – BGN

Sirianni is hardly the only coach who doesn’t ace game management. Look at Liam Coen! The Jags didn’t have a great day in that regard. But Coen provided value for his team with his contributions as an offensive mind. Sirianni isn’t bringing that to the table. Outside of player motivation, I’m not really sure what edge Sirianni is giving his team. Rather, he’s been a liability. And, make no mistake, he WILL be held accountable for the Eagles’ struggles if they continue. Especially as it relates to their offensive woes:

NFC East Mixtape Vol. 197: The NFC Least is back! – NFC East Mixtape

It only took five weeks into this NFL season, but the NFC Least is officially BACK! Despite two of the teams playing one another, not a single NFC East team won in Week 5. What’s more is that there were some particularly embarrassing moments. The Dallas Cowboys got destroyed by a winless Tampa Bay Buccaneers team while the Philadelphia Eagles blew a lead with 8 seconds in London against the Jacksonville Jaguars. The New York Giants might feel okay to have salvaged a tie, but they owe Jayden Daniels and Dan Quinn a huge thanks as that duo really let down the Washington Commanders. RJ Ochoa and Brandon Lee Gowton discuss it all! You can see that we have a BRAND NEW NFC East Mixtape YouTube Channel so make sure to subscribe as the show will live here exclusively in video format. AND you can also listen to the show! On Blogging The Boys and/or Bleeding Green Nation podcast feeds as well as the SB Nation NFL Show feed!

NFL winners and losers: The NFC East has become football’s saddest division – SB Nation

As a whole, the NFC East is a combined 8-10-2. Not the worst division on paper but it owns some of the most embarrassing losses in the NFL so far. Their collective schedules are only getting more difficult from here, and we could easily see three coaches get axed from the East before the season finishes — unless there’s some demonstrable improvement. This shouldn’t happen in the NFC East. Routinely, it’s one of the league’s better conferences, home to some of the richest rivalries, and with more trash talking than most of football combined. Instead of talking trash to each other, these teams can only point to how trash they have become.

Panthers vs. Eagles odds: Opening lines for Week 6 matchup – Cat Scratch Reader

Remember that home-field advantage is traditionally accounted for by spotting the home team—theEagles, in this case—three points on the spread. That would actually see the Panthers favored by less than a safety on a neutral field. It is clear that FanDuel doesn’t trust Bryce Young yet. Honestly, that’s kind of fair, but this still feels like a betting line weighted more on performance from past seasons for both teams than it is on the last four to five games of the 2026 season.

3 Numbers to Know From the Jaguars’ Win Over the Eagles – Big Cat Country

6%. That was Jacksonville’s win probability with eight seconds left in the game, per NFL Pro. Jake Elliot had just knocked through a 48-yard field goal to put the Eagles up by one point. If the Jaguars had any timeouts remaining, they might’ve been able to pick up a chunk completion before stopping the clock and attempting a lengthy walk-off field goal. But the Jaguars didn’t have any timeouts, and the Eagles made sure they’d have even less time by kicking off short of the endzone to prevent a touchback. Then Ameer Abdullah happened.

Some Good Signs – Iggles Blitz

Let’s move past the fact the Eagles lost to the Jags. That was a horrible outcome, but there are some real positives to take away from the game. There are absolutely some things to build upon moving forward. The defense started to look more like what we expected. Jalen Carter played his best game in a while, finishing with 5 tackles, 2 sacks, 2 FF, 1 TFL, and a PD. He also drew a holding call (finally!). Carter created at least one TFL for a teammate (Coop). He was a disruptive force. This defense is completely different when Carter plays like that.

‘It hasn’t been good enough:’ Sirianni searching for answers for woeful offense – NBCSP

No, they’re not the worst offense in the NFL. They’re just 28th in scoring, 31st in yards, 22nd on third down, 30th in yards per play, 28th in passing, 23rd in rushing and 26th in sacks allowed and 32nd in first downs. Five weeks into the 2026 season, the Eagles’ offense is among the worst in the league in every significant category. And it’s getting worse. Over the last three weeks, the Eagles are last in most of those categories. During their three-game losing streak, the Eagles have averaged 14.7 points and 217 yards per game, averaged 3.98 yards per play, recorded 39 first downs and converted 22.2 percent of their third downs. All worst or 2nd-worst in the league during that span. Last time the Eagles were that bad in all those categories in any three-game span was the first three games of 1999, Andy Reid’s first year as an NFL head coach with Doug Pederson as his quarterback. But that was a rebuilding team coming off a 3-13 season in 1998 with a first-time head coach and a rookie quarterback in Donovan McNabb who would soon take over. This is a team that came into the season with legit Super Bowl aspirations that’s made the playoffs five straight years and had a top-10 offense every year from 2022 through 2024.

Nick Sirianni defends Eagles’ late clock management, regrets kickoff decision vs. Jaguars – The Athletic

Sirianni had the wrong takeaway from the end of the game. Comparatively speaking, the kickoff decision was more defendable than the approach that left to leaving time on the clock.

Elliott came onto the field with 12 seconds remaining. Had the Eagles snapped the ball for Elliott’s field-goal attempt with two seconds remaining, a successful kick would have ended the game. But Sirianni stood by the way he handled that final sequence. “You’d love for the last play of the game to be your kick, but you’d also say, ‘Hey, if I can get that clock under 20 seconds, you’re accomplishing that as well,’” Sirianni said. “Leading into that last play, I said what I said yesterday. I stand by that. I did not make the decision that I wanted to make there in that particular case, and it cost us. There’s nothing else to be said about that.”

Nick Sirianni, Jalen Hurts seems to disagree on the management of Philly’s final drive – PFT

If Lemon had simply fallen down in bounds, it wouldn’t have been an issue. The Jaguars would have used their final timeout, and the Eagles could have run the ball, called a timeout with three or four seconds left, and kicked a walk-off field goal. Is that on Lemon? Is it on the coaching staff for calling a play that put the ball so close to the sideline? Is it on Hurts for throwing to a player who was near the sideline, when he had a man wide open on the thirty-two at the left hash? Regardless, Sirianni has no regrets as to how things played out before the final kickoff. Hurts apparently does. It’ll be interesting to monitor that dynamic if other questions regarding game management, play-calling, etc. emerge as the year moves forward.

Bowen: The Eagles went from ‘How did they win this?’ To ‘How did they lose this,’ and nothing good seems to last for this team – PHLY Eagles

As Nick Sirianni said, “I didn’t make the right decision, and I lost us that game.” You’ve probably heard that he said that by now, you don’t need me to tell you, but some quotes just have to make the column. It was rare for Sirianni to jettison the coachy cliches and speak from the heart. It also was impossible to disagree. His outmanned players lurched to the improbable edge of victory. And he couldn’t seal the deal. A team with an offensive line of Jordan Mailata, Willie Lampkin, Jake Majors, Tyler Steen and Markel Bell somehow mounted a 32-yard field goal drive in the final seconds against the NFL’s best defense, using nine plays to do so, with fourth-string running back Dameon Pierce. That Elliott field goal represented the Eagles’ first second-half points in three games. As painful as the game was to watch, it would have been one of the signature drives of Jalen Hurts’ career, a win that would bring all kinds of hope to a struggling team that still hopes to get a bunch of injured stars back and compete for the NFC East. Yes, the Jags played down to the Eagles’ level, taking 13 penalties, sometimes seeming to actively avoid scoring. But the win was right there. Eight seconds left. Instead, as one Eagle muttered in the locker room, “We’re 2-3. We should be 4-1.” (I’m not identifying him because although reporters were around, he was talking to a teammate.)

2026 NFL season, Week 5: What We Learned from Sunday’s games – NFL.com

Eagles’ nightmare month gets worse, but OL, DL hold up. Philly’s week from hell saw it lose three potential starting offensive linemen (Lane Johnson to retirement, Cam Jurgens to Baltimore, Drew Kendall to injury). The Eagles entered Sunday with Saquon Barkley and DeVonta Smith sidelined, too, to injury. It didn’t get any easier for Philadelphia against Jacksonville. The Eagles lost their RB3, Will Shipley, to a foot injury after he scored the game-opening TD, then lost emerging pass rusher Jalyx Hunt (ankle/knee) on the final play of the first half. And yet, for the majority of Sunday’s action, Philly held its own on the line of scrimmage. Jalen Carter led a resilient defensive effort, notching two strip-sacks of Trevor Lawrence in the first half, though Philly couldn’t cash in on either of those fumbles. Carter was one of five defenders with at least three pressures. The Eagles’ two goal-line stands were heroic and kept the game within reach. On the other side of the ball, Jacksonville logged pressures on 54.8% of Jalen Hurts’ dropbacks but notched just one sack against a MacGyvered offensive line. For a Philly team in disarray, its third straight loss and the manner in which it lost it will inspire panic in the city, but this is a roster, when healthy, that can compete with the best in the league and contend for the postseason. The Eagles’ resiliency showed on Sunday (that is, until the very end).

Eagles schedule could be changing after disappointing start – Inquirer

The Eagles, who have lost three straight, find themselves with a losing record for the first time under head coach Nick Sirianni. It also doesn’t help that the Birds have had an unwatchable second-half offense where the star has been punter Braden Mann. The Commanders are even worse, with just one win after an inexplicable collapse in overtime Sunday against the New York Giants (3-1-1). As a result, the NFL is considering whether to flex Eagles-Commanders off NBC and replace it with a better matchup. The league has until Oct. 20 to make a final decision, so it will depend what happens this weekend. The Eagles face the Carolina Panthers (2-2) at home in Week 6, while the Commanders face the undefeated San Francisco 49ers (5-0) Monday night on ESPN.

Spadaro: Nick Sirianni knows ‘our job is to get up and keep fighting’ – PhiladelphiaEagles.com

He also talked about the ensuing kickoff with eight seconds remaining on the clock, one that Jacksonville running back Ameer Abdullah returned 52 yards to set up Cam Little’s 57-yard field goal. Sirianni said he had “regret” not having Elliott kick off through the end zone, which would have given the Jaguars a first down at their 35-yard line with eight seconds remaining on the clock and no timeouts. “To give them back the ball with eight seconds left, I think we did what we needed to do as an offense, and you obviously saw the success of Jake’s (field goal) in that particular case,” Sirianni said. Sirianni and his coaching staff and players continue to work on improving all phases of the team, saying his coaching staff’s “job is to figure it out. We’ve got to find solutions. That’s our job. Plain and simple. Period.” That, Sirianni said, pertains to the offense, defense, special teams, and every aspect of the Philadelphia Eagles.

Browns add another former Broncos RB with Quinshon Judkins hurt, reportedly – Dawgs By Nature

The head coach reported that Dylan Sampson could be brought back from injured reserve soon but, according to multiple reports, the Browns are signing [former Eagles] RB Audric Estime to their active roster as well.

Jameis Winston is, and should be, the NY Giants quarterback – Big Blue View

Can we stop now with the breathless drum-banging for J.J. McCarthy to replace Jameis Winston as quarterback of the New York Giants sooner rather than later? The Giants unquestionably lose Sunday’s game against the Washington Commanders without Winston’s heroics — 254 yards passing and three touchdowns, two of those in the final eight minutes of regulation to erase a 14-point deficit, and the first 50+ pass game of his 12-year career without an interception. Albeit, the last fact comes with help from a questionable call. Winston, as he reminded reporters recently, is the Giants’ starting quarterback. With Jaxson Dart gone for the season, he deserves to be.

History says this Cowboys team is doomed – Blogging The Boys

Of the previous 2-3 instances where a Cowboys team was 2-3 or worse through the first five games, they have only made the playoffs twice. If we round up that is 9%. You’ll note that each of those two teams (1996 and 2018) saw the Cowboys reach the postseason as the NFC East winner. Some years it pays to be in a crummy division, and that certainly seems to be the case this year for Dallas. On the heels of what we saw in Week 5, 10 wins probably earns some hats and t-shirts for whoever gets there. Maybe it will be the Cowboys. But this does not bode well! If you look at the list of teams on this list and reference them against what you remember about each of them, you will realize that we are talking about some Cowboys teams that were not very good and who were actually particularly maddening.

Commanders vs. Giants (game one) – Studs and Duds – Hogs Haven

Dan Quinn (and David Blough) — Head coach Dan Quinn laid yet another egg, this time with the game hanging in the balance. The clock management, play calling and lack of decision-making has grown old. If Blough was the one who called a pass play in that situation, I don’t know why Quinn didn’t override that. At this point, Quinn is nothing more than an overpaid cheerleader.

item.title: TreVeyon Henderson to miss ‘multiple weeks’ with reported high ankle sprain
item.description: The Patriots running back hurt his ankle during Sunday’s win over the Raiders.
item.content:encoded:
The New England Patriots offense has taken another hit. Running back TreVeyon Henderson, who was unable to finish Sunday’s win over the Las Vegas Raiders, has been diagnosed with a high ankle sprain.

The injury will sideline him for “multiple weeks,” according to a report by Adam Schefter of ESPN. The Patriots are, however, hoping for a return “sooner rather than later.”

Henderson, 23, left the game against the Raiders in the second quarter. He was tackled from behind on an 11-yard jet sweep and remained on the ground injured. After gingerly departing for the locker room, he was initially announced as questionable to return to the contest but never actually reemerged.

In his absence, the Patriots turned to starting running back Rhamondre Stevenson and third-stringer Corey Kiner. Stevenson and Kiner combined to gain 116 rushing yards on just 19 carries against the Raiders, averaging 6.1 yards per carry and scoring a touchdown. Kiner also lost a fumble on his first touch of the game, New England’s only turnover in a 45-17 victory.

Henderson originally joined the Patriots as a second-round draft pick in 2025. The Ohio State product finished his rookie campaign with a combined 1,241 scrimmage yards and 10 touchdowns in 21 games.

In 2026 so far, he has carried the ball 42 times for 163 yards and a score. He also caught two passes for an extra 22 yards.

The Patriots will host the New York Jets at Gillette Stadium this Sunday for a 1 p.m. ET kickoff.

item.title: Eagles' Jordan Mailata reflects on team's offensive line losses, London game collapse: 'A week from hell'
item.description: Jordan Mailata found a way to perfectly describe how the Eagles were feeling after their loss to the Jaguars in London.
item.content:encoded:
The Philadelphia Eagles are in a tailspin. Following the sudden retirement of Lane Johnson, the trade of Cam Jurgens and the last-second loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars in London, Eagles players are not having a good time right now.

No one understands that more than offensive tackle — and team captain — Jordan Mailata. The seven-year veteran did not mince words when asked whether the Eagles can take anything away from Sunday's loss, saying it's been "a week from hell" for the team, per NBC Sports Philadelphia.

"My brain hurts. This week has been a week from hell for me. I don't even know the concept of a moral victory right now. I'm just trying to look internally to see how I contributed to this loss so I can correct it. We weren't good enough. We know that."

Mailata's comments came after two of his closest teammates — Johnson and Jurgens — left the Eagles. It also came after the team flew all the way to London just to lose on a literal last-second field goal.

While Mailata was frustrated with himself after he was called for a false start during the game, he hasn't been the problem for the Eagles this season. Mailata ranks as the fifth-best offensive tackle this season, per Pro Football Focus' metrics. He's been a consistent positive on the Eagles since jumping into a starting role in 2020.

Though Mailata's comments sound depressing, he offered a simple solution for moving on, saying he would watch the film, chat with his teammates and turn the page on the week.

Things won't get much easier for the Eagles moving forward. The team will take on the emergent Carolina Panthers in Week 6 before playing all three division opponents from Week 7 through Week 9.

Given the team's 2-3 start, this upcoming stretch could define the team's 2026 season. With a strong showing over the next four weeks, the Eagles should stay in the playoff hunt. But if things start to snowball, there could be many more hellish weeks on the horizon for Mailata and the Eagles moving forward.

item.title: Cowboys DC Christian Parker will coach from the booth rather than the sideline
item.description: The Cowboys brought Mike Pettine in as a senior defensive assistant on Monday and that's not the only change they'll be making as they try to improve their defensive performance over the final 12 games.
item.content:encoded:
The Cowboys brought Mike Pettine in as a senior defensive assistant on Monday and that's not the only change they'll be making as they try to improve their defensive performance over the final 12 games.

During an appearance on 105.3 The Fan on Tuesday, Cowboys owner Jerry Jones said that the team has been searching "for what we can do differently that would give us better results." One of the things they've settled on is moving defensive coordinator Christian Parker from the sideline to the booth on gamedays.

"We’re gonna coach the defense not on the field, but up above. Parker’s going up above," Jones said.

Jones said that the changes are not a sign that they believe Parker is overwhelmed in his first year as the coordinator, but the defense has looked overwhelmed far too often and Jones will eventually run out of levers to pull in hopes of finding a way to fix a unit that the team expected to be much better than it has been thus far.

item.title: Brian Branch precedent points to a suspension for Alaric Jackson
item.description: The Rams may not have left tackle Alaric Jackson for Sunday's game against the Cardinals.
item.content:encoded:
The Rams may not have left tackle Alaric Jackson for Sunday's game against the Cardinals. And not because of an injury.

Jackson's decision to punch Bills defensive end Bradley Chubb in the face well after the game ended invites a suspension.

Last year, the NFL imposed a one-game suspension on Lions safety Brian Branch for striking Chiefs receiver JuJu Smith-Schuster with an open hand to the facemask in the immediate aftermath of a Sunday night game.

“Your aggressive, non-football act was entirely unwarranted, posed a serious risk of injury, and clearly violated the standards of conduct and sportsmanship expected of NFL players,” NFL V.P. of football operations Jon Runyan wrote in a letter to Branch, exactly one year ago to the day. “Your conduct reflected poorly on the NFL and has no place in our game.”

On Monday night, Jackson sucker punched Chubb well after the game ended; Chubb's helmet was off, and Jackson had returned to the field after removing his shoulder pads and jersey.

If it had happened outside the stadium, Jackson would have been arrested and charged with assault. (He still could be, technically.) The fact that it happened well after the Monday night game ended could prompt scrutiny under the Personal Conduct Policy, which prohibits (among other things) "[v]iolent or threatening behavior toward another employee or a third party in any workplace setting."

If the NFL proceeds under the Personal Conduct Policy, Jackson's prior violation could prompt something more than a one-game suspension.

Either way, discipline is surely coming for Jackson. Given the precedent set by the Brian Branch case, the punishment should be a suspension of at least one game.

UPDATE 11: 47 a.m. ET: Per the NFL, it's not a Personal Conduct Policy issue. Jackson will be subject to discipline under the normal pregame/in-game/postgame rules.

item.title: NFL Week 6 betting: 5 biggest storylines, including Rams still being favored to win Super Bowl
item.description: The Rams' loss on Monday night dropped their record to 2-3 this season.
item.content:encoded:
It was a remarkably balanced Week 5 in the NFL, from a betting perspective.

Before Monday night's game, seven favorites and seven underdogs had covered (favorites went 7-6-1 if you score the closing line for Bengals-Dolphins at Cincinnati -7 instead of -7.5). There were also seven unders and seven overs. In the Monday night game the Bills won as underdogs, evening up the underdogs' record at 7-7-1 if the Dolphins were counted as a push, and the game went over. Oddsmakers know how to set lines, especially when it comes to the NFL.

Here are the top five betting storylines for Week 6 of the NFL season:

Rams on top of Super Bowl odds

Monday night brought one of the most exciting games of the season, and a 2-3 start for the Rams after they lost in overtime to the Bills. You'd think that would drop them down in the Super Bowl odds. Not so.

The Rams are still favored to win the Super Bowl at BetMGM as of Tuesday morning, at +700 odds. The Bills and 49ers are next at +750. The Rams are also favored at FanDuel at +700 odds, with the Ravens and Bills tied for second at +750. The Rams and 49ers are tied for the best Super Bowl odds at DraftKings, with each team at +700.

The Rams' schedule does get easier, but they already trail the 49ers by three games in the NFC West. They have been one of the NFL's most disappointing teams so far, considering what was expected from them. But the current market shows that oddsmakers are unwilling to boost the Rams' odds up, worrying about having a lot of exposure if they finally live up to the preseason hype.

Eagles still favored

The Eagles are 2-3, have not looked good yet this season and will be playing immediately after a game in London. They're facing the Carolina Panthers, who are rested after a bye.

And the Eagles are still favored. It's not by much, which shows how the Eagles have slipped. They're 1-point favorites early in the week. That's also some respect for the Panthers, who are playing very well on offense and are 2-2 to start the season.

Many road favorites

There could be some interesting games in Week 6. There are plenty of small road favorites, or home teams that are barely favored.

In eight of the 13 games with a true home team (the Jaguars and Texans play in London, while four teams have byes), the road team is either favored or a 1-point underdog. The biggest road favorite is the Bills, who are -7 at the Raiders. Las Vegas was the last undefeated team against the spread, but failed to cover in Week 5 as it got blown out by the Patriots.

It could be a wild week around the NFL.

Giants getting no respect

The Giants are 3-1-1 and in first place of the (putrid) NFC East. That 3-1-1 record doesn't hold much weight in the betting market.

The Saints are 1-4, with the only win coming on a fourth-quarter rally at Baltimore. The last two weeks they lost by 21 at home to the Falcons and by 10 at home to the Vikings, gaining only 142 yards against Minnesota. And still, the Saints are 1-point road favorites at the Giants.

That sums up the state of the NFC East through five games.

High scoring Sunday night?

The Sunday night game has two flawed teams, but it still could be fun.

The Packers and Cowboys are the Sunday night game. The Cowboys are 2-3 and the Packers are 3-2. Each have their issues, including defense. Especially for Dallas. That's why the total is 52.5. The only other total on the board higher than that is Bills-Raiders at 53.

The Cowboys' defense ranks 32nd in DVOA and Packers quarterback Jordan Love just had a huge game against the Bears. We know the Cowboys can move the ball, and the Packers defense was below average before a big game against Chicago in Week 5. It could be an exciting Sunday night game.
